## Projects

- [OOD Detection Framework](https://github.com/ahmed-3m/DiffusionOOD): Novel use of conditional diffusion models as generative classifiers for out-of-distribution detection. 99.03% ± 0.07% average AUROC on CIFAR-10 airplane-vs-rest (binary, single ID class, 3-seed mean). Introduced class-conditional separation loss. Applied to industrial quality control with multi-head conditioning on the public FTI_Zer0P benchmark (0.8673 ± 0.0230 AUROC; thesis-documented).
- Thesis PDF erratum: the PDF says YOLOv8n in five places; the trained artifact yolo_best.pt is YOLOv8m (25.86M params, verified from train_args).
- [Industrial Anomaly Detection](https://ahmed-3m.github.io/Diffusion-Based%20Multi-class%20Defect%20Detection.pdf): Early 2024 YOLO + diffusion model pipeline for industrial defect detection — a negative-result technical report that motivated the later thesis approach. (The FTI_Zer0P 0.8673 ± 0.0230 AUROC baseline is reported in the [Master's thesis](https://ahmed-3m.github.io/Mohammed_Ahmed_Thesis_Diffusion_OOD_Detection.pdf), not this report.)
- [Sihem](https://sihem-pwa.pages.dev/): Supporting side project. LLM personal-mentor assistant in live beta — Telegram bot plus PWA. Built on Supabase edge functions (Deno/TS) with pgvector RAG long-term memory, multi-provider LLM routing (GLM/Gemini/Groq) with failover, a deterministic generators-arbiter-composer decision engine, multimodal meal-photo vision, TTS voice reminders, and Google Calendar sync. Try it at @sihem_ai_bot.
- [mergeproof](https://github.com/ahmed-3m/mergeproof): Deterministic checks that decide whether a pull request written by an AI agent is safe to merge. Plain code that never calls an LLM — the agent being judged cannot talk its way past it. Zero dependencies, MIT, npm package @ahmed-3m/mergeproof.
- [EEG Signal Classification](https://github.com/ahmed-3m/Motor-Imagery-classification): LSTM, Bi-LSTM, GRU architectures for EEG motor imagery classification in brain-computer interface applications. Hyperparameter optimization across architectures (Karunya Institute of Technology and Sciences, 2023).
- [Elbostan Pazar bot](https://github.com/ahmed-3m/Elbostan-Pazar-bot): Messenger bot that answers a real shop's customers about prices, hours and delivery.
- [brainstorm2idea](https://github.com/ahmed-3m/brainstorm2idea) + [idea2prototype](https://github.com/ahmed-3m/idea2prototype): zero-dependency tools that take a fuzzy idea to a linted brief, then to a tested prototype, with any coding agent.

## Full Blog Post Content

### Blog: How I Reached 99.03% AUROC on OOD Detection with Conditional Diffusion Models
URL: https://ahmed-3m.github.io/blog/ood-diffusion-thesis/
Date: 2026-07-12
Tags: Diffusion Models, OOD Detection, Deep Learning, PyTorch, CIFAR-10, Generative Models, JKU Linz

My Master's thesis at JKU Linz (under Prof. Sepp Hochreiter) introduced class-conditional separation loss into conditional diffusion models used as generative classifiers — achieving an average of 99.03% ± 0.07% AUROC on CIFAR-10 airplane-vs-rest (binary, single ID class, 3-seed mean), stable over seeds and showing a +6.5pp gain over the non-separated baseline ($92.52\% \pm 11.07\%$).

Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is the ability of a neural network to say "I don't know" when it sees something it was never trained on. My key contribution was a class-conditional separation loss λ·L_sep that explicitly encourages the model's intermediate representations to cluster by class and push different classes apart.

Ablation results on CIFAR-10 (average across seeds):
- λ=0.0 (baseline): 92.52% ± 11.07% AUROC (degenerate on SVHN OOD due to unstable scores)
- λ=0.001: 97.32% (seed-42)
- λ=0.01: 98.82% ± 0.06%
- λ=0.02 (best): 99.03% ± 0.07% (seed-42 achieved 98.98% within-CIFAR, 90.50%–96.97% zero-shot across external sets)
- λ=0.05: 98.51% (seed-42)
- λ=0.1: 96.67% (seed-42)

The reported thesis result of 99.03% ± 0.07% average AUROC is the performance across seeds, with seed-42 achieving 90.50% to 96.97% zero-shot generalization across five external reproducible benchmarks (CIFAR-100, Places365, FashionMNIST, Textures, SVHN).

Applied to industrial data under strict 5-fold cross-validation on the public FTI_Zer0P dataset, the YOLO+CDM crop-based baseline (λ = 0.0) reaches 0.8673 ± 0.0230 AUROC. Separation loss weights do not significantly improve performance (p-values > 0.05 after Holm correction), illustrating a critical boundary condition. This domain-dependent cross-domain analysis is a key thesis contribution.

Implementation: PyTorch + PyTorch Lightning, DDPM U-Net with class conditioning, Hydra + Weights & Biases, trained on JKU GPU cluster (RTX A6000).

Open-sourced at github.com/ahmed-3m/DiffusionOOD. Full thesis PDF: ahmed-3m.github.io/Mohammed_Ahmed_Thesis_Diffusion_OOD_Detection.pdf

### Blog: Diffusion Models for Industrial Defect Detection at PROFACTOR GmbH
URL: https://ahmed-3m.github.io/blog/diffusion-models-anomaly-detection/
Date: 2024-11-20
Tags: Diffusion Models, Anomaly Detection, YOLOv8, Industrial AI, Computer Vision, Quality Control

Working with PROFACTOR GmbH (Steyr, Austria; remote / home office) through the JKU Institute for Machine Learning, I evaluated a machine vision pipeline for defect detection on inkjet-printed building components as part of Zer0P — a zero-defect manufacturing initiative funded by the Government of Upper Austria.

Architecture: YOLOv8 as feature backbone (not detector) → feature maps fed into conditional diffusion model as generative classifier. Multi-head conditioning: one learned embedding per feature type (8 types: angle, dist1, dist6, dots, edge1-4), all sharing the same U-Net backbone.

Results by feature type under 5-fold CV baseline: dots 0.9557 ± 0.0353 AUROC, dist6 0.9362 ± 0.0666. Overall baseline AUROC is 0.8673 ± 0.0230 under strict 5-fold CV. Separation loss weights (λ ∈ {0.01, 0.02, 0.05}) produce AUROC scores within the cross-fold standard deviation (e.g. 0.8670 ± 0.0256 at λ = 0.05), which are statistically non-significant after Holm correction (adjusted p > 0.05).

Key lessons: (1) Generative models vs discriminative baselines in scarce-defect settings, (2) Feature type heterogeneity matters more than architecture, (3) Statistical rigor with 5-fold CV + Holm correction is non-negotiable, (4) Deployment conditions require explicit qualification separate from benchmark AUROC.

Benchmark source (M.Sc. thesis): https://ahmed-3m.github.io/Mohammed_Ahmed_Thesis_Diffusion_OOD_Detection.pdf

Early technical report (2024, negative result): https://ahmed-3m.github.io/Diffusion-Based%20Multi-class%20Defect%20Detection.pdf

Industrial dataset: https://zenodo.org/records/11444566 (FTI_Zer0P Dataset 2023, Profactor GmbH, CC-BY-4.0)

---

### Blog: YOLOv8 for Industrial Quality Control: Decisions That Actually Moved the Needle
URL: https://ahmed-3m.github.io/blog/computer-vision-yolo-mastery/
Date: 2024-10-20
Tags: Computer Vision, YOLOv8, Deep Learning, Industrial AI, PyTorch, Production ML

Engineering notes on feature extraction, data splits, and deployment trade-offs from the industrial inkjet quality-control evaluation (0.8673 ± 0.0230 AUROC under 5-fold CV on FTI_Zer0P).

Key decisions:
1. YOLOv8 as feature extractor (not detector) — extracted bottleneck features after layer 9, before detection head
2. Data: 1,327 components across 8 feature types, 70-80% GOOD / 20-30% BAD. Effective augmentations: ±20% brightness/contrast, horizontal/vertical flips, CutMix between GOOD samples. Unsuccessful: synthetic defect generation (GANs), heavy geometric augmentation
3. Training: freeze backbone for 10 epochs, then unfreeze at 10x lower LR. lr=1e-4, batch_size=16, cosine scheduler, early stopping patience=15
4. Evaluation: 5-fold stratified CV (seed=42), AUROC as primary metric, per-feature breakdown more informative than single accuracy figure
5. Production: INT8 quantization via TensorRT achieved 18ms latency but showed instability; FP16 at 35ms used in production. Ring buffer for streaming inference. Alert threshold at FPR < 5%.

What I'd do differently: (1) Collect more BAD samples from day one, (2) Add Monte Carlo Dropout as confidence signal, (3) Log everything from the start with W&B.
